issues.description: Good explanation that --stats with --quiet searches all files completely, but doesn't explain the performance implications clearly
issues.current_content: Note: When combining `--stats` with `--quiet`, ripgrep will search all files completely to collect accurate statistics, even though `--quiet` alone would normally exit after the first match.
issues.should_add: Explain that this means --stats overrides the early-exit optimization of --quiet, which can significantly impact performance on large searches
issues.fix_suggestion: Expand the note: 'This means --stats disables --quiet's early-exit optimization. If you're just checking for pattern existence in a large codebase, using both flags together will be much slower than --quiet alone, as it must search all files to completion.'
issues.source_reference: crates/printer/src/summary.rs:126-135, 673-675 - quit_early() check is bypassed when stats are enabled

issues.description: Chapter shows the stats object structure but doesn't document the 'human' field in elapsed_total
issues.current_content: Shows elapsed_total with only secs and nanos fields in the JSON example
issues.should_be: Should document that elapsed_total also includes a 'human' field with formatted time string for readability
issues.fix_suggestion: Add to the JSON example after line 162: "human": "0.001000s" field in elapsed_total object, and mention it in the description

issues.description: Example shows thread time calculation but doesn't clearly explain why/when thread time aggregation happens or what it indicates
issues.current_content: Example shows '4 threads × 0.1s each = 0.400000 seconds' but mechanism is implicit
issues.should_add: Clarify that 'seconds spent searching' is the sum of all thread CPU time, which naturally exceeds wall-clock time in parallel execution
issues.fix_suggestion: Expand explanation: 'The "seconds spent searching" metric accumulates CPU time across all threads. With parallel search, this will typically exceed wall-clock time. A ratio close to your thread count indicates good parallelization. For example, if you have 4 threads and the ratio is ~4x, your search is efficiently using all threads.'
issues.source_reference: crates/printer/src/stats.rs:31-34, 71-74 - elapsed() returns Duration and add_elapsed() accumulates across all searches/threads

issues.description: Doesn't explain multiline match behavior for matched_lines count
issues.current_content: - **Matched lines**: Number of unique lines containing matches
issues.should_be: - **Matched lines**: Number of lines containing matches. For multiline patterns (-U), all lines participating in a match are counted.
issues.fix_suggestion: Update description to: '- **Matched lines**: Number of lines containing matches. Note: With multiline patterns (--multiline or -U), this counts all lines that participate in or are part of any match, not just the first line of each match.'
issues.source_reference: crates/printer/src/stats.rs:56-62 - 'When matches may contain multiple lines then this includes every line that is part of every match'

issues.description: Shell script example uses fragile text parsing instead of recommending the more robust JSON format
issues.current_content: Shows grep/cut parsing of text output
issues.should_add: Recommend using --json --stats for scripts, which is more reliable and structured
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add a note before the example: 'For production scripts, prefer JSON output for reliable parsing:' and then add a second example:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
OUTPUT=$(rg --json --stats 'pattern' | tail -1)
MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.data.stats.matches')
FILES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.data.stats.searches_with_match')
echo "Found $MATCHES matches across $FILES files"
```
issues.source_reference: crates/core/main.rs:445-458 - JSON stats output is structured and reliable for parsing

issues.description: Doesn't mention the minimal performance overhead of --stats itself
issues.should_add: Note that --stats has negligible performance overhead - it's safe to use in performance-sensitive contexts
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a note at the end of the Performance Metrics section: 'The --stats flag itself has minimal performance overhead since ripgrep tracks these metrics internally regardless. Enabling --stats only adds the cost of formatting and printing the final summary.'
issues.source_reference: crates/printer/src/stats.rs - Stats tracking is lightweight, just incrementing counters
